sources.quote: formed well in laboratory settings, excitement about their potential has been tempered by concerns

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: that these tools are prone to “hallucination,” and may produce coherent sounding but inaccurate

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: information (Peng et al., 2023a; Roose, 2023).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: In this paper, we study the adoption of a generative AI tool that provides conversational guidance

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: for customer support agents.1 This is, to our knowledge, the ﬁrst study of the impact of generative

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: AI when deployed at scale in the workplace. We ﬁnd that access to AI assistance increases the

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: productivity of agents by 14 percent, as measured by the number of customer issues they are able to

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: resolve per hour. In contrast to studies of prior waves of computerization, we ﬁnd that these gains

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: accrue disproportionately to less-experienced and lower-skill workers.2 We argue that this occurs

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: because ML systems work by capturing and disseminating the patterns of behavior that characterize

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: the most productive agents.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: Computers and software have transformed the economy with their ability to perform certain

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: tasks with far more precision, speed, and consistency than humans. To be eﬀective, these systems

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: typically require explicit and detailed instructions for how to transform inputs into outputs: when

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: engineers write code to perform a task, they are codifying that task. Yet because many production

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: processes rely on tacit knowledge, these processes have so far deﬁed automation (Polanyi, 1966;

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: Autor, 2014).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: Machine learning algorithms work diﬀerently. In contrast to traditional programming, these

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: systems implicitly infer instructions from examples. Given a training set of images, for instance,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: ML systems can learn to recognize faces. This highlights a key, distinguishing aspect of ML systems:

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: they can learn to perform tasks even when no instructions exist–including tasks requiring tacit

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: knowledge that could previously only be gained through lived experience (Polanyi, 1966; Autor,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: 2014; Brynjolfsson and Mitchell, 2017).3

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: We study the impact of generative AI on productivity in the customer service sector, an indus-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote: try with one of the highest rates of AI adoption (Chui et al., 2021). We examine the staggered

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote:
1A note on terminology. There are many deﬁnitions of artiﬁcial intelligence and of intelligence itself— Legg et
al. (2007) list over 70 of them. In this paper, we deﬁne “artiﬁcial intelligence” (AI) as an umbrella term that refers
to a computer system that is able to sense, reason, or act like a human. “Machine learning” (ML) is a branch of AI
that uses algorithms to learn from data, identify patterns and make predictions or decisions without being explicitly
programmed (Google, n.d.). Large language models (LLMs) and tools built around LLMs such as ChatGPT are
an increasingly important application of machine learning. LLMs generate new content, making them a form of
“generative AI.”

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 2 页
sources.quote:
2We provide a discussion of this literature at the end of this section.
3As Meijer (2018) puts it “where the Software 1.0 Engineer formally speciﬁes their problem, carefully designs algo-
rithms, composes systems out of subsystems or decomposes complex systems into smaller components, the Software
2.0 Engineer amasses training data and simply feeds it into an ML algorithm...”

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: deployment of a chat assistant using data from 5,000 agents working for a Fortune 500 software

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: ﬁrm that provides business process software. The tool we study is built on a recent version of the

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT) family of large language models developed by OpenAI

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: (OpenAI, 2023). It monitors customer chats and provides agents with real-time suggestions for how

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: to respond. It is designed to augment agents, who remain responsible for the conversation and are

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: free to ignore its suggestions.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: We have four sets of ﬁndings.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: First, AI assistance increases worker productivity, resulting in a 13.8 percent increase in the

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: number of chats that an agent is able to successfully resolve per hour. This increase reﬂects shifts in

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: three components of productivity: a decline in the time it takes to an agent to handle an individual

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: chat, an increase in the number of chats that an agent is able to handle per hour (agents may handle

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: multiple calls at once), and a small increase in the share of chats that are successfully resolved.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: Second, AI assistance disproportionately increases the performance less skilled and less experi-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: enced workers across all productivity measures we consider. In addition, we ﬁnd that the AI tool

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: helps newer agents move more quickly down the experience curve: treated agents with two months

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: of tenure perform just as well as untreated agents with over six months of tenure. These results

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: contrast, in spirit, with studies that ﬁnd evidence of skill-biased technical change for earlier waves

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: of computer technology (Autor et al., 2003; Acemoglu and Restrepo, 2018; Bresnahan et al., 2002;

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: Bartel et al., 2007).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: Our third set of results investigates the mechanism underlying our ﬁndings so far. We posit that

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: high-skill workers may have less to gain from AI assistance precisely because AI recommendations

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: capture the potentially tacit knowledge embodied in their own behaviors. Rather, low-skill workers

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: are more likely to improve by incorporating these behaviors by adhering to AI suggestions. Consis-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: tent with this, we ﬁnd few positive eﬀects of AI access for the highest-skilled or most-experienced

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: workers. Instead, using textual analysis, we ﬁnd suggestive evidence that AI assistance leads lower-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: skill agents to communicate more like high-skill agents.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: Finally, we show that the introduction of AI systems can impact the experience and organization

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: of work. We show that AI assistance markedly improves how customers treat agents, as measured

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: by the sentiments of their chat messages. This change may be associated with other organizational

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: changes: turnover decreases, particularly for newer workers, and customers are less likely to escalate

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: a call by asking to speak to an agent’s supervisor.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: Our overall ﬁndings demonstrate that generative AI working alongside humans can have a sig-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 3 页
sources.quote: niﬁcant positive impact on the productivity and retention of individual workers. We emphasize,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: however, that our paper is not designed to shed light on the aggregate employment or wage eﬀects

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: of generative AI tools.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: Our paper is related to a large literature on the impact of various forms of technological adoption

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: on worker productivity and the organization of work (e.g. Rosen, 1981; Autor et al., 1998; Athey

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: and Stern, 2002; Bresnahan et al., 2002; Bartel et al., 2007; Acemoglu et al., 2007; Hoﬀman et al.,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: 2017; Bloom et al., 2014; Michaels et al., 2014; Garicano and Rossi-Hansberg, 2015; Acemoglu and

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: Restrepo, 2020). Many of these studies, particularly those focused on information technologies, ﬁnd

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: evidence that IT complements higher-skill workers (Akerman et al., 2015; Taniguchi and Yamada,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote:
2022).
Bartel et al. (2007) shows that ﬁrms that adopt IT tend to use more skilled labor and

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: increase skill requirements for their workers. Acemoglu and Restrepo (2020) study the diﬀusion of

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: robots and ﬁnd that the negative employment eﬀects of robots are most pronounced for workers

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: in blue-collar occupations and those with less than a college education. In contrast, we study a

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: diﬀerent type of technology—generative AI—and ﬁnd evidence that it most eﬀectively augments

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: lower-skill workers.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: For example, Peng et al. (2023b) recruit software engineers for a speciﬁc coding task (writing an

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: HTTP server in JavaScript) and show that those given access to GitHub Copilot complete this task

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: twice as quickly. Similarly, Noy and Zhang (2023) run an online experiment showing that subjects

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: given access to ChatGPT complete professional writing tasks more quickly. In addition, they show

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: that ChatGPT compresses the productivity distribution, with lower-skill workers beneﬁting the

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: To the best of our knowledge, however, there have been no studies of the impact of access to gen-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: erative AI tools on productivity in real-world workplaces, nor over longer periods. Such studies are

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: important because the impact of AI on productivity may vary over time and interact with workers’

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: baseline level of experience or expertise. Technologies that look promising in laboratory settings

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: may have more limited eﬀects in practice because of the need for complementary organizational

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: investments, skill development and business process redesign. In addition, the introduction of AI

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: systems may have further impacts on worker and customer satisfaction, attrition, and patterns of

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: organizational behavior.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote:
1
Generative AI and Large Language Models

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: In recent years, the rapid pace of AI development and public release tools such as ChatGPT,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: GitHub Copilot, and DALL-E have attracted widespread attention, optimism, and alarm (The

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 4 页
sources.quote: White House, 2022). These technologies are all examples of “generative AI,” a class of machine

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: learning technologies that can generate new content—such as text, images, music, or video—by

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: analyzing patterns in existing data. In this section, we provide background on generative AI as a

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: technology and discuss its potential economic implications.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote:
1.1
Technical Primer

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: In this paper, we focus on an important class of generative AI, large language models (LLMs). At

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: a high level, LLMs are neural network models designed to process sequential data (Bubeck et al.,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: 2023). For instance, an LLM can be trained by giving it access to a large corpus of text (such

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: as Wikipedia, digitized books, or portions of the Internet) and using that input text to learn to

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: predict the next word in a sequence, given what has come before. This knowledge of the statistical

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: co-occurrence of words allows it to generate new text that is grammatically correct and semantically

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: meaningful.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: Though the name implies human language, the same techniques can be used to produce LLMs

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: that generate other forms of sequential data such as protein sequences, audio, computer code, or

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: chess moves (Eloundou et al., 2023).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: Recent progress in generative AI has been driven by four factors: computing power, earlier

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: innovations in model architecture, the ability to “pre-train” using large amounts of unlabeled data,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote:
and reﬁnements in training techniques.4
Model performance depends strongly on scale, which

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: includes the amount of computing power used for training, the number of model parameters, and

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: dataset size (Kaplan et al., 2020). Pre-training an LLM requires thousands of GPUs and weeks to

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: months of dedicated training time. For example, estimates indicate that a single training run for a

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: GPT-3 model with 175 billion parameters, trained on 300 billion tokens, may cost $5 million dollars

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: in just computing costs (Li, 2020; Brown et al., 2020).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: In terms of model architecture, modern LLMs make use of two earlier key innovations: positional

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: encoding and self-attention. Positional encodings keep track of the order in which a word occurs

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: in a given input.5 This allows large bodies of input text to be broken into smaller segments that

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: can be processed simultaneously without “forgetting” earlier parts of the input (Vaswani et al.,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: 2017; Bahdanau et al., 2015). Meanwhile, self-attention assigns importance weights to each word

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: in the context of the entire input text. Older approaches that assign importance based on word

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: frequencies that may misrepresent a word’s true semantic importance. These older methods may

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: also base on semantic content within a small window. In contrast, self-attention enables models to

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote:
4For a more detailed technical review of progress, see Radford and Narasimhan (2018); Radford et al. (2019); Liu
et al. (2023); Ouyang et al. (2022).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 5 页
sources.quote: 5For instance, a model would keep track of “the, 1” instead of only “the” (if “the” was the ﬁrst word in the sentence).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: capture long-range semantic relationships within an input text, even when that text is broken up

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: and processed in parallel (Vaswani et al., 2017).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: Second, LLMs can be pre-trained on large amounts of unlabeled data. For instance, GPT is

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: trained on unlabeled text data, allowing it to learn patterns in human language without explicit

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote:
guidance (Radford and Narasimhan, 2018).
Because unlabeled data is far more prevalent than

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: labeled data, this allows for LLMs to learn about natural language on a much larger training corpus

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: (Brown et al., 2020). The resulting model can be used in multiple applications because its training

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: is not speciﬁc to a particular set of tasks.6

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: Finally, general-purpose LLMs can be further “ﬁne-tuned” to generate output that matches the

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: priorities of any speciﬁc setting (Ouyang et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2023). For example, an LLM may

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: generate several potential responses to a given query, but some of them may be factually incorrect

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: or biased. To discipline this model, human evaluators can rank these outputs to train a reward

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: function prioritizes some responses over others. Such reﬁnements can signiﬁcantly improve model

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: quality but making a general-purpose model better suited to its speciﬁc application (Ouyang et al.,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: Together, these innovations have generated meaningful improvements in model performance.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: The Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT) family of models, in particular, has attracted con-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: siderable media attention for their rapidly expanding capabilities.7

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote:
1.2
The Economic Impacts of Generative AI

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: Computers have historically excelled at executing pre-programmed instructions, making them par-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: ticularly eﬀective at tasks that can be standardized and reduced to explicit rules (Autor, 2014).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: Consequently, computerization has had a disproportionate impact on jobs that involve routine

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: tasks, such as data entry, bookkeeping, and assembly line work, and reducing demand for workers

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: performing “routine” tasks (Acemoglu and Autor, 2011). At the same time, computerization has

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: also increased the productivity of workers who possess complementary skills, such as programming,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: data analysis, and research. Together, these changes have contributed to increasing wage inequality

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: in the United States and have been linked to a variety of organizational changes (Katz and Murphy,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: 1992; Autor et al., 2003; Michaels et al., 2014; Bresnahan et al., 2002; Baker and Hubbard, 2003).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: In contrast, recent advances in AI, particularly those driven by generative AI, suggest that it

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote: is possible for LLMs to perform a variety of non-routine tasks such as software coding, persuasive

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote:
6For example, a model trained to generate tweets based on the history of Twitter will diﬀer depending on whether
its inputs are labeled with each tweet’s number of retweets or an assessment of its truthfulness.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 6 页
sources.quote:
7For instance, GPT-4 has recently been shown to outperform humans in taking the US legal bar exam (Liu et al.,
2023; Bubeck et al., 2023; OpenAI, 2023).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: writing, and graphic design (Bommasani et al., 2021; Eloundou et al., 2023). For example, Copilot,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: an AI pair programmer that generates code suggestions for programmers, has achieved impressive

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: performance on technical coding questions and generates an average of 46 percent of code among

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: users (Nguyen and Nadi, 2022; Zhao, 2023). Similarly, services like Elicit and Casetext use LLMs to

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: ﬁnd and summarize key information in legal documents or research, tasks that were previously con-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: sidered non-routine (Elicit, 2023; Casetext, 2023). Since many of these tasks are currently performed

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: by workers who have either been insulated or beneﬁted from prior waves of technology adoption,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: the expansion of generative AI has the potential to shift the relationship between technology, labor

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: productivity, and inequality (The White House, 2022).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: Unlike traditional programming, generative AI does not require explicit instructions as inputs.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: Instead, it uses ML to mine vast amounts of human-generated data to recognize patterns, allowing

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: it to generate, summarize, and make inferences based on those patterns. For instance, if prompted

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: to provide a cover for a gothic novel, generative AI models will respond with an illustration that is

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: moody; if asked to write an email denying an employee a raise, generative AI will respond with a

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: note that is professional; this occurs even though no programmer has instructed the AI model as to

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: what tone would be appropriate in a given context. The ability to behave “appropriately” cannot

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: be reduced to a set of rules; instead people learn to do so from experience and apply unconscious

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: rules in the process. The fact that generative AI models display such skills suggests that they have

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: the potential to move past what has been termed “Polanyi’s Paradox,” the idea that knowledge is

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: diﬃcult to codify because individuals perform many tasks they cannot articulate (Polanyi, 1966;

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: Autor, 2014).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: At the same time, LLMs have signiﬁcant limitations. Popular LLM-based tools such as ChatGPT

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: have been shown to produce false or misleading information in unpredictable ways. While these

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: models often perform well on speciﬁc tasks in the lab, these concerns have raised questions about

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: their ability to perform well in more complex real-world settings (Peng et al., 2023a).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote:
2
Our Setting: LLMs for Customer Support

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote:
2.1
Customer Support and Generative AI

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: We study the impact of generative AI in the customer service industry, an area with one the highest

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote: surveyed rates of AI adoption.8 Customer support interactions are important for maintaining a

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 7 页
sources.quote:
8For instance, of the businesses that report using AI, 22 percent use AI in their customer service centers (Chui et
al., 2021).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: company’s reputation and building strong customer relationships, yet as in many industries, there

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: is substantial variation in worker productivity (Berg et al., 2018; Syverson, 2011).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: Newer workers are also often less productive and require signiﬁcant training. At the same time,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: turnover is high: industry estimates suggest that 60 percent of agents in contact centers9 leave each

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: year, costing ﬁrms $10,000 to $20,000 dollars per agent (Buesing et al., 2020; Gretz and Jacobson,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: 2018). To address these workforce challenges, the average supervisor spends at least 20 hours per

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: week coaching lower-performing agents (Berg et al., 2018). Faced with variable productivity, high

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: turnover, and high training costs, ﬁrms are increasingly turning toward AI tools (Chui et al., 2021).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: At a technical level, customer support is well-suited for current generative AI tools. From an

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: AI’s perspective, customer-agent conversations can be thought of as a series of pattern-matching

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: problems in which one is looking for an optimal sequence of actions. When confronted with an issue

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: such as “I can’t login,” an AI/agent must identify which types of underlying problems are most likely

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: to lead a customer to be unable to log in and think about which solutions typically resolve these

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: problems (“Can you check that caps lock is not on?”). At the same time, they must be attuned to

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: a customer’s emotional response, making sure to use language that increases the likelihood that a

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: customer will respond positively (“that wasn’t stupid of you at all! I always forget to check that

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: too!”). Because customer service conversations are widely recorded and digitized, pre-trained LLMs

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: can be ﬁne-tuned for customer service using many examples of both successfully and unsuccessfully

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: resolved conversations.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: In the remainder of this section, we provide details about the ﬁrm we study and the AI tool

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: they adopt.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote:
2.2
Data Firm Background

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: We work with a company that provides AI-based customer service support software (hereafter, the

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: “AI ﬁrm”) to study the deployment of their tool at one of their client ﬁrms, (hereafter, the “data

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: Our data ﬁrm is a Fortune 500 enterprise software company that specializes in business process

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote:
software for small and medium-sized businesses in the United States.
It employs a variety of

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: chat-based technical support agents, both directly and through third-party ﬁrms. The majority of

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: agents in our sample work from oﬃces located in the Philippines, with a smaller group working in

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: the United States and in other countries. Across locations, agents are engaged in a fairly uniform

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote: job: answering technical support questions from US-based small business owners.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 8 页
sources.quote:
9The term “contact center” updates the term “call center,” to reﬂect the fact that a growing proportion of customer
service contacts no longer involve phone calls.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: Chats are randomly assigned and support sessions are relatively lengthy, averaging 40 minutes

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: with much of the conversation spent trying to diagnose the underlying technical problem. The job

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: requires a combination of detailed product knowledge, problem-solving skills, and the ability to deal

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: with frustrated customers.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: Our ﬁrm measures productivity using three metrics that are standard in the customer service

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: industry: “average handle time,” the average length of time an agent takes to ﬁnish a chat; “resolution

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: rate,” the share of conversations that the agent can successfully resolve; and “net promoter score,”

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: (customer satisfaction), which are calculated by randomly surveying customers after a chat and

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: calculating the percentage of customers who would recommend an agent minus the percentage who

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: would not. A productive agent is one who is able to ﬁeld customer chats quickly while maintaining

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: a high-resolution rate and net promoter score.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: Across locations, agents are organized into teams with a manager that provides feedback and

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: training to agents. Once per week, managers hold one-on-one feedback sessions with each agent.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: For example, a manager might share the solution to a new software bug, explain the implication of

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: a tax change, or suggest how to better manage customer frustration with technical issues. Agents

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: work individually and the quality of their output does not directly aﬀect others. Agents are paid

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: an hourly wage and bonuses based on their performance relative to other agents.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote:
2.3
AI System Design

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: The AI system we study uses a generative model system that combines a recent version of GPT

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: with additional ML algorithms speciﬁcally ﬁne-tuned to focus on customer service interactions. The

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: system is further trained on a large set of customer-agent conversations that have been labeled with

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: a variety of outcomes and characteristics: whether the call was successfully resolved, how long it

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: took to handle the call, and whether the agent in charge of the call is considered a “top” performer

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: by the data ﬁrm. The AI ﬁrm then uses these data to look for conversational patterns that are

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: most predictive of call resolution and handle time.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: The AI ﬁrm further trains its model using a process similar in spirit to Ouyang et al. (2022) to

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: prioritize agent responses that express empathy, surface appropriate technical documentation, and

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: limit unprofessional language. This additional training mitigates some of concerns associated with

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: relying on LLMs to generate text.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: Once deployed, the AI system generates two main types of outputs: 1) real-time suggestions for

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: how agents should respond to customers and 2) links to the data ﬁrm’s internal documentation for

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: relevant technical issues. In both cases, recommendations are based on a history of the conversation.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 9 页
sources.quote: For example, the correct response when a customer says “I can’t track my employee’s hours during

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: business trips” depends on what version of the data ﬁrm’s software the customer uses. Suppose

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: the customer has previously mentioned that they are using the premium version. In that case,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: they should have access to remote mobile device timekeeping, meaning that the support agents

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: need to diagnose and resolve a technical issue preventing the software from working. If, however,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: the customer stated that they are using the standard version, then the correct solution is for the

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: customer to upgrade to the premium version in order to access this feature.10

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: Figure 1 illustrates sample output. In the chat window (Panel A), Alex, the customer, describes

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: their problem to the agent. Here, the AI assistant generates two suggested responses (Panel B). In

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: this example, it has learned that phrases like “I can deﬁnitely assist you with this!” and “Happy to

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: help you get this ﬁxed asap” are associated with positive outcomes. Panel A of Appendix Figure

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: A.1 shows an example of a technical recommendation from the AI system, which occurs when it

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: recommends a link to the data ﬁrm’s internal technical documentation.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: Importantly, the AI system we study is designed to augment, rather than replace, human agents.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: The output is shown only to the agent, who has full discretion over whether to incorporate (fully or

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: partially) the AI suggestions. This reduces the potential for output that is oﬀ-topic or incorrect to

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: make its way into customer conversations. Furthermore, the system does not provide suggestions

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: when it has insuﬃcient training data for that situation (this occurs in a large minority of cases). In

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: these situations, the agent must respond on their own.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: Finally, we observe that the AI model is trained on human-generated data in a setting where

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: there is high variability in the abilities of individual agents. As a result, when the model identiﬁes

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: patterns that distinguish successful from unsuccessful calls, it is implicitly learning the diﬀerences

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: that characterize high- versus low-skill workers. For example, top-performing agents are often more

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: eﬀective at diagnosing the underlying technical issue given a customer’s problem description: in an

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: internal study, our AI ﬁrm found that top performers start researching a solution twice as quickly

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: as the average workers. An AI system, with access to many examples of diagnostic questions and

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: eventual solutions, may be able to encode some of the “best practices” top-performing agents use.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: This suggests that an AI system may be able to more eﬀectively share knowledge across workers

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: both because it may capture tacit knowledge that was previously diﬃcult for managers to articulate

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: and because it can provide more real-time recommendations than a busy manager.11 Indeed, AI

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote: recommendations can be thought of as expanding the marginal productivity of high-skill workers

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 10 页
sources.quote:
10For more on context tracking, see, for instance, Dunn et al. (2021).
11By necessity, managers can only base their feedback on a small subset of the hundreds of conversations an agent
conducts. And because managers are often pressed for time and may lack training, they may focus on a single metric
(“you need to solve problems faster”) rather than identifying strategies for how an agent could better approach a
problem (“you need to ask more questions at the beginning to diagnose the issue better.”) This type of coaching is
ineﬀective and often counterproductive for employee engagement (Berg et al., 2018).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: by encoding their conversational patterns and disseminating them to other workers. In our setting,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: high-skill workers are not compensated for these contributions.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote:
3
Deployment, Data, and Empirical Strategy

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote:
3.1
AI Model Deployment

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: The AI assistant we study was gradually rolled out at the agent level after an initial seven-week

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: randomized pilot featuring 50 agents.12 The deployment was largely uniform across both the data

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote:
ﬁrm’s own customer service agents, as well as its outsourced agents.
Figure 2 documents the

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: progression of deployment among agents who are eventually treated. The bulk of the adoption

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: occurs between November 2020 and February 2021.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote:
3.2
Summary Statistics

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: Table 1 provides details on sample characteristics, divided into three groups: agents who are never

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: given access to the AI tool during our sample period (“never treated”), pre-AI observations for

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: those who are eventually given access (“treated, pre”), and post-AI observations (“treated, post”).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: In total, we observe the conversation text and outcomes associated with 3 million chats by 5,179

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: agents. Within this, we observe 1.2 million chats by 1,636 agents in the post-AI period. Most agents

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: in our sample, 83 percent, are located outside the United States, primarily in the Philippines. For

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: each agent, we observe their assigned manager, tenure, geographic location and ﬁrm information.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: To examine the impacts of this deployment, we construct several key variables, all aggregated

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: to the agent-month level, which is our primary level of analysis.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: Our primary measure of productivity is resolutions per hour (RPH), the number of chats that

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: a worker is able to successfully resolve per hour. We consider this measure to be the most eﬀective

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: summary of a worker’s productivity at the ﬁrm. An agent’s RPH is determined by several factors:

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: the average time it takes an agent to complete a conversation, the number of conversations they

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: are able to handle per hour (accounting for multiple simultaneous conversations), and the share of

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: conversations that are successfully resolved. We measure these individually as, respectively, average

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: handle time (AHT), chats per hour (CPH), and resolution rate (RR). In addition, we also observe

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: a measure of customer satisfaction through an agent’s net promoter score (NPS), which is collected

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote: by the ﬁrm from post-call customer surveys.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 11 页
sources.quote:
12Data from the RCT is included as part of our primary analysis but is not analyzed separately because of its small
sample size.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: We observe these measures for diﬀerent numbers of agents. In particular, we are able to re-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: construct measures of average handle time and chats per hour from our chat level data. Therefore

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: we observe AHT and CPH measures for all agents in our sample. Measures that involve an un-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: derstanding of call quality—resolution rates, and customer satisfaction—are provided at the agent

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: month level by our data ﬁrm. Because our data outsources most of its customer service functions,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: it does not have direct control over this information, which is kept by subcontracted ﬁrms. As a

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: result, we observe resolution rates and net promoter scores for a subset of agents in our data. This,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: in turn, means that we only observe our omnibus productivity measure—resolutions per hour—for

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: this smaller subset.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: Figure 3 plots the raw distributions of our outcomes for each of the never, pre-, and post-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: treatment subgroups. Several of our main results are readily visible in these raw data. In Panels

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: A through D, we see that post-treatment agents have higher outcomes than both never-treated

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: agents and pre-treatment agents. In Panel E, we see no discernible diﬀerences in surveyed customer

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: satisfaction among pre- and post-AI groups.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: Focusing on our main productivity measure, Panel A of Figure 3 and Table 1 show that never-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: treated agents resolve an average of 1.7 chats per hour whereas post-treatment agents resolve 2.5

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: chats per hour. Some of this diﬀerence may be due to diﬀerences in the initial section: treated

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: agents have higher resolutions per hour prior to AI model deployment (2.0 chats) relative to never

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: treated agents (1.7). This same pattern appears for other outcomes: chats per hour (Panel C) and

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: resolution rates (Panel D). Panel B illustrates the clearest pattern with average handle times: both

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: pre-treatment and never-treated agents had a similar distribution of average handle times, centered

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: at 40 minutes but post-treatment agents have a lower average handle time of 35 minutes.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote:
3.3
Empirical Strategy

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: We isolate the causal impact of access to AI recommendations using a standard diﬀerence-in-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: diﬀerences regression model:

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote:
yit “ δt ` αi ` βtAIit ` γXit ` ϵit
(1)

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: Our outcome variables yit capture average handle times, resolution rates, resolutions per hour, and

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: customer satisfaction scores for agent i in year-month t. Because workers often work only for a

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: portion of the year, we include only year-month observations for an agent who is actively employed

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: (e.g. assigned to chats). Our main variable of interest is AIit, an indicator equal to one if agent

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 12 页
sources.quote: i has access to AI recommendations at time t. All regressions include year-month ﬁxed eﬀects δt

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 13 页
sources.quote: to control for common, time-varying factors such as tax season or business quarter end. In our

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 13 页
sources.quote: preferred speciﬁcation, we also include controls for time-invariant agent-level ﬁxed eﬀects αi and

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 13 页
sources.quote: time-varying agent tenure. Standard errors are clustered at the agent or agent-location level.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 13 页
sources.quote: A rapidly growing literature has shown that two-way ﬁxed eﬀects regressions deliver consistent

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 13 页
sources.quote: estimates only with strong assumptions about the homogeneity of treatment eﬀects, and may be

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 13 页
sources.quote: biased when treatment eﬀects vary over time or by adoption cohort (Cengiz et al., 2019; de Chaise-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 13 页
sources.quote: martin and D’Haultfœuille, 2020; Sun and Abraham, 2021; Goodman-Bacon, 2021; Callaway and

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 13 页
sources.quote: Sant’Anna, 2021; Borusyak et al., 2022). For instance, workers may take time to adjust to using the

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 13 页
sources.quote: AI system, in which case its impact in the ﬁrst month may be smaller. Alternatively, the onboarding

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 13 页
sources.quote: of later cohorts of agents may be smoother, so that their treatment eﬀects may be larger.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 13 页
sources.quote: We study the dynamics of treatment eﬀects using the interaction weighted (IW) estimator pro-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 13 页
sources.quote: posed in Sun and Abraham (2021). Sun and Abraham (2021) show that this estimator is consistent

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 13 页
sources.quote: assuming parallel trends, no anticipatory behavior, and cohort-speciﬁc treatment eﬀects that follow

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 13 页
sources.quote: the same dynamic proﬁle.13 In the Appendix, we show that both our main diﬀerences-in-diﬀerences

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 13 页
sources.quote: and event study estimates are similar using robust estimators introduced in de Chaisemartin and

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 13 页
sources.quote: D’Haultfœuille (2020), Borusyak et al. (2022), Callaway and Sant’Anna (2021), and Sun and Abra-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 13 页
sources.quote: ham (2021), as well as using traditional two-way ﬁxed eﬀects OLS.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 13 页
sources.quote:
4
Results

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 13 页

4.1
