sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 14 页
sources.quote:
4.2
Impacts by Agent Skill and Tenure

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 14 页
sources.quote: As discussed earlier, generative AI tools may have a diﬀerent pattern of productivity consequences

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 14 页
sources.quote: relative to earlier waves of technology adoption.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: In Panel A of Figure 6, we consider how our estimated productivity eﬀects diﬀer by an agent’s

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: pre-AI productivity. We divide agents into quintiles using a skill index based on their average call

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: eﬃciency, resolution rate, and surveyed customer satisfaction in the quarter prior to the adoption

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: of the AI system. These skill quintiles are deﬁned within a ﬁrm-month. In Panel A, we show that

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: the productivity impact of AI assistance is most pronounced for workers in the lowest skill quintile

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: (leftmost side), who see a 35 percent increase in resolutions per hour. In contrast, AI assistance

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: does not lead to any productivity increase for the most skilled workers (rightmost side).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: In Figure 7 we show that less-skilled agents consistently see the largest gains across our other

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: outcomes. For the highest-skilled workers, we ﬁnd mixed results: a zero eﬀect on average handle time

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: (Panel A), a positive eﬀect for calls per hour (Panel B), and, interestingly, small but statistically

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: signiﬁcant decreases in resolution rates and customer satisfaction (Panels C and D). These ﬁndings

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: suggest that while lower-skill workers improve from having access to AI recommendations, they may

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: distract the highest-skilled workers, who are already doing their jobs eﬀectively.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: Next, in Panel B of Figure 6, repeat this analysis for tenure by dividing agents into ﬁve groups

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: based on their tenure at the time that the AI model is introduced. Some agents have less than one

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: month of tenure when they receive AI access, while others have over a year of experience. We see a

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: clear, monotonic pattern in which the least experienced agents see the greatest gains in resolutions

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: per hour.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: In Figure 8, we show that these patterns persist for other outcomes: AI assistance generates

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: larger gains in call handling and quality for the newest workers. For more experienced workers,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: we ﬁnd positive eﬀects for average handle time and calls per hour (Panels A and B), zero eﬀects

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: on resolution rate (Panel C), and a small but statistically signiﬁcant negative eﬀect for customer

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: satisfaction (Panel D).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: In Appendix Figures A.3 and A.4, we show that our skill-heterogeneity results are robust to

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: controlling for agent tenure, and vice versa. This suggests the AI system has distinct impacts both

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: by worker experience and ability.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote:
4.3
Moving Down the Experience Curve

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: To further explore how AI assistance impacts newer workers, we examine how worker productivity

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: evolves on the job.14 In Figure 9, we plot productivity variables by agent tenure for three distinct

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote: groups: agents who never receive access to the AI model (“never treated”), those who have access

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 15 页
sources.quote:
14We avoid the term “learning curve” because we cannot distinguish if workers are learning or merely following
recommendations.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: from the time they join the ﬁrm (“always treated”), and those who receive access in their ﬁfth month

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: with the ﬁrm (“treated 5 mo.”).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote:
We see that all agents begin with around 2.0 resolutions per hour.
Workers who are never

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: treated slowly improve their productivity with experience, reaching approximately 2.5 resolutions

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: 8 to 10 months later. In contrast, workers who begin with access to AI assistance rapidly increase

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: their productivity to 2.5 resolutions only two months in. Furthermore, they continue to improve

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: at a rapid rate until they are resolving more than 3 calls an hour after ﬁve months of tenure.15

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: Comparing just these two groups suggests that access to AI recommendations helps workers move

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: more quickly down the experience curve.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: The ﬁnal line in Panel A tracks workers who begin their tenure with the ﬁrm without access to

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: AI assistance, but who receive access after ﬁve months on the job. These workers improve slowly in

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: the same way as never-treated workers for the ﬁrst ﬁve months of their tenure. Starting in month

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: ﬁve, however, these workers gain access and we see their productivity rapidly increase following

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: the same trajectory as the always-treated agents. In Appendix Figure A.5, we plot these curves

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: for other outcomes. We see clear evidence that the experience curve for always-treated agents is

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: steeper for handle time, chats per hour, and resolution rates (Panels A through C). Panel D follows

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: a similar but noisier pattern for customer satisfaction.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: Taken together, these results indicate that access to AI helps new agents move more quickly

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: down the experience curve. Across many of the outcomes in Figure 9, agents with two months of

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: tenure and access to AI assistance perform as well as or better than agents with more than six

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: months of tenure who do not have access.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote:
4.4
Adherence to AI recommendations

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: We emphasize that the AI tool we study is meant to augment— rather than replace—human agents.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: The system makes suggestions, but agents may elect to ignore these suggestions entirely. In our

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: results above, we estimate intent-to-treat eﬀects, that is how access to the AI tool impacts outcomes

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: regardless of how frequently agents follow its recommendations. In this section, we examine how

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: closely agents adhere to AI recommendations, and document the association between adherence and

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: returns to adoption.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: We measure “adherence” starting at the chat level, by calculating the share of AI recommen-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: dations that each agent follows. Agents are coded as having adhered to a recommendation if they

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: either click to copy the suggested AI text or if they self-input something very similar. We then

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: aggregate this to the agent-month level.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 16 页
sources.quote: 15Our sample ends here because we have very few observations more than ﬁve months after treatment.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: Panel A of Figure 10 plots the distribution of average agent-month-level adherence for our

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: post-AI sample, weighted by the log of the number of AI recommendations given to that agent in

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: that month. The average adherence rate is 38 percent with an interquartile range of 23 percent

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: to 50 percent: agents frequently ignore recommendations. In fact, the share of recommendations

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: followed is similar to the share of other publicly reported numbers for generative AI tools; a study

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: of GitHub Copilot reports that individual developers use 27 to 46 percent of code recommendations

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: (Zhao, 2023). Such behavior could be optimal: the AI model may make incorrect or non-sensical

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: suggestions.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: Panel B of Figure 10 shows that returns to AI model deployment tend to be higher among

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: agents who follow a greater share of recommendations. We divide agents into quintiles based on the

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: percent of AI recommendations they follow in the ﬁrst month of deployment and separately estimate

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: the impact of access to the AI model for each group. These estimates control for year-month and

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: agent ﬁxed eﬀects as in Column 5 of Table 2.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: For agents in the lowest quintile of adherence, we still see a 10 percent gain in productivity, but

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: for agents in the highest quintile, the estimated impact is much higher, close to 25 percent. Appendix

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: Figure A.6 shows the results for our other four outcome measures. The positive correlation between

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: adherence and returns holds most strongly for average handle time (Panel A) and calls per hour

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: (Panel B), and more noisily for resolution rate (Panel C) and customer satisfaction (Panel D).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: We note that this relationship could be driven by a variety of factors: the treatment eﬀect

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: of adherence (agents have greater productivity because they listen to recommendations); selection

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: (agents who choose to adhere are more productive for other reasons); or selection on gains (agents

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: who follow recommendations are those with the greatest returns).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: Finally, Figure 11 plots how adherence to AI recommendations evolves for workers of diﬀerent

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: experience or skill. In Panel A, we see that more senior workers are initially less likely to follow AI

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: recommendations: 30 percent for those with over a year of tenure compared to 37 percent for those

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: with under three months of tenure.16 Over time, however, all workers increase their adherence, with

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: more senior workers doing so faster so that the groups converge ﬁve months after tenure. In Panel

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: B, we see a similar but more muted pattern for worker skill: lower-skill workers are initially more

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: likely to comply, but the highest-skilled workers converge over time.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: These ﬁndings are consistent with both the possibility that workers who are initially more

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: skeptical may come to see the value of AI recommendations over time or that workers who strongly

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: dislike working with the AI system may exit at higher rates. Other studies on the use of AI tools

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: have found diﬀerences in the desire to follow AI recommendations; for instance, in a study of a

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 17 页
sources.quote: 16Agents below three months of experience are in their “onboarding” phase.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: writing suggestion tool, Singh et al. (2022) ﬁnds that four of the 23 study participants refused to

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: engage with AI suggestions.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote:
4.5
Textual Evidence

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: Our evidence so far suggests that access to AI suggestions improves productivity and, for the lower-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: skilled and less-experienced agents, increases conversation quality as measured by resolution rates

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: and surveyed customer satisfaction.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: Next, we consider why AI may have these impacts. This section provides evidence from prelim-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: inary analysis of the textual content of chat conversations. Our goal is to understand whether and

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: how AI recommendations change the way agents communicate.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: In particular, we are interested in AI model’s ability to encode the potentially tacit knowledge of

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: high performers: does AI assistance lead lower-skill workers to communicate more like higher-skill

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: workers? Because tacit knowledge is, by deﬁnition, not something that can be codiﬁed as a set of

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: rules, we examine the overall textual similarity of conversations rather than looking for the presence

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: of speciﬁc formulaic phrases.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: We begin by constructing textual embeddings of agent-customer conversations. These embed-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: dings allow us to represent their semantic and stylistic content as a vector so that we can compare

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: one conversation to another using cosine similarity. Cosine similarity is a widely-used metric for

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: measuring the similarity of two embeddings. It calculates the cosine of the angle between two n-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: dimensional vectors, where values close to 1 indicate similarity (Koroteev, 2021). We form our text

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: embeddings using all-MiniLM-L6-v2, an LLM that is speciﬁcally intended to capture and cluster

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: semantic information in order to assess similarity (Hugging Face, 2023). We then compare how an

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: agent’s conversations change over time (e.g. within-person similarity over time), as well as how high-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: and low-skill agents’ conversations compare with each other over time (between-person similarity

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: at a given point in time).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote:
4.5.1
Within-worker changes in communication

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: To examine how AI changes agent conversations with customers, we begin by comparing an individ-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: ual agent’s text pre- and post-AI model deployment. We take a given agent’s corpus of text from

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: an eight-week window before deployment and compare it with text from the same-sized window af-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: terward. We exclude the three weeks around deployment to account for disruptions due to training

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: and individual adjustment to the AI model. We exclude messages from the customer, and focus

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: only on agent-generated language. Then, for each individual agent, we plot textual dissimilarity be-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 18 页
sources.quote: tween pre- and post-AI conversations as one minus the cosine similarity. The within-person textual

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: diﬀerence in our data is roughly 0.3, indicating that, on average, agents continue to communicate

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: similarly after the deployment of the AI model. For context, the sentences “Can you help me with

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: this logging in?” and “Why is my login not working?” have a cosine similarity of 0.68.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: We examine how language changes pre- and post-AI for workers who are initially high- and low-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: skill, where high-skill workers are deﬁned as those in the top quintile of the skill index distribution,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: while low-skill workers are those in the bottom quintile.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: If the AI is able to embody and disseminate some of the tacit “best practices” of high-skill

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: workers, then we would expect low-skill workers to experience a greater shift in communication

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: patterns following access to AI assistance (high-skill workers would change less since the AI model is

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: suggesting practices they have already adopted). In Panel A of Figure 12, we ﬁnd evidence consistent

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: with this hypothesis: initially lower-skill agents shift their language more after AI model deployment,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: relative to initially higher-skill workers. The scores we plot include controls for conversation timing

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: to account for seasonal changes in topics such as tax season or payroll cycles. These results also

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: control for agent tenure to account for the possibility that younger workers’ language may evolve

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: more quickly independent of access to the AI model.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: If AI assistance merely leads workers to type the same things but faster, then we would not

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: expect this diﬀerential change. And because chats are randomly allocated to agents, we would not

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: also expect the pattern we document to be driven by diﬀerential changes in conversation topics

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: between high and low-skill workers.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote:
4.5.2
Across worker comparisons

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: We next explore how lower-skill agents’ language choices change with AI assistance. In Panel B of

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: Figure 12, we provide suggestive evidence that AI assistance leads lower-skill agents to communicate

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: more like high-skill agents. In particular, we plot the cosine similarity between high- and low-skill

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: agents at speciﬁc moments in calendar time, separately for workers with (blue dots) and without

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: (red diamonds) access to AI assistance. Among agents without access, we deﬁne high- and low-skill

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: agents as those who are in the top or bottom quintile of our skill index for that month. Among

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: agents with access, we deﬁne high- and low-skill agents based on whether they are in the top or

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: bottom quintile of skill at the time of deployment.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: Focusing on the blue dots, we see that the average textual similarity between high- and low-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: productivity workers is 0.55. This ﬁgure is lower than our average within-person text similarity

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: (0.73), which makes sense given that these are across-person comparisons. Textual similarity is

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 19 页
sources.quote: stable over time, suggesting that high- and low-skill workers are not trending diﬀerently in the

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: absence of the AI assistant. Turning to the red diamonds, post-AI, the textual similarity between

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: high- and low-skill workers increases.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: Combined with our results from Panel A, this suggests that low-skill workers are converging

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: toward high-skill workers, rather than the opposite. The magnitude of this change—moving from

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: 0.55 similarity to 0.61 similarity—may appear small, but given that the average within-person

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: similarity for high-skill workers is 0.73, this result suggests that AI assistance is associated with a

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: substantial narrowing of language gaps.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote:
4.6
Eﬀects on the Experience and Organization of Work

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: Access to AI assistance may impact workers and the ﬁrm organization as a whole through changes in

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: work experience, turnover, and task allocation. In this section, we examine some of these outcomes.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote:
4.6.1
Sentiment

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: Customers often vent their frustrations on anonymous service agents and, in our data, we see regular

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: instances of swearing, verbal abuse, and “yelling” (typing in all caps). A key part of agents’ jobs is

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: to absorb customer frustrations while restraining one’s own emotional reaction (Hochschild, 2019).

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: The stress associated with this type of emotional labor is often cited as a key cause of burnout and

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: attrition among customer service workers (Lee, 2015). It is unclear what impact AI assistants may

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: have on the tenor of conversations: AI recommendations may help the agent more eﬀectively set the

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: customer’s expectations or resolve their problem, but customers may react poorly if AI-suggested

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: language feels “corporate” or insincere.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: To assess this, we attempt to capture the aﬀective nature of both agent and customer text, using

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: sentiment analysis (Mejova, 2009). For this analysis, we use SiEBERT, an LLM that is ﬁne-tuned

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: for sentiment analysis using a variety of datasets, including product reviews and tweets (Hartmann

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: et al., 2023). Sentiment is measured on a scale from ´1 to 1. We compute sentiment scores for

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: the agent and customer text of each chat separately, and then aggregate across all chats for each

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: agent-year-month.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: Panels A and B of Figure 13 describe the distributions of average customer and visitor sentiment

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: scores. On average, customer sentiments in our data are mildly positive and normally distributed

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: around a mean of 0.14 except for a mass of very positive and very negative scores. As one might

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: expect, customer service agents are trained to be extremely positive and professional so agent

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: sentiment scores are almost always highly positive, with a mean of 0.89.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: Panels C and D consider how sentiment scores respond to the introduction of the AI assistant.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 20 页
sources.quote: In Panel C, we see an immediate and persistent improvement in customer sentiment. This eﬀect is

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: economically large: according to Column 1 of Table 4, access to AI improves the mean customer

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: sentiments (averaged over an agent-month) by 0.18 points, equivalent to half of a standard deviation.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: We see a much smaller impact on agent scores. In Panel D, we see no detectable eﬀect for agent

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: sentiment, which unsurprising because agent’s expressed sentiment is already very high. Column 2

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: of Table 4 indicates that agent sentiments increase by only 0.02 points or about one percent of a

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: standard deviation.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: Appendix Figure A.7 examines heterogeneity sentiment impacts, by agent tenure and skill.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: Consistent with our main results, we ﬁnd that most sentiment improvements occur for workers with

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: lower tenure and skills at the time of deployment. In contrast with our productivity results, the

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: eﬀects on customer sentiments are broader and no longer necessarily monotonic in tenure or skill.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: We ﬁnd the largest eﬀects for workers with 3-6 months of tenure at AI model deployment, and we

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: ﬁnd a smaller impact of AI on sentiments only for agents in the highest quintile skill. These results

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: suggest that AI recommendations, which were explicitly designed to prioritize more empathetic

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: responses, may improve agents’ social skills and have a positive emotional impact on customers.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote:
4.6.2
Attrition

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: Increases in worker-level productivity do not always lead workers to be happier with their jobs. If

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: workers become more productive but dislike being managed by an AI assistant, this may lead to

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: greater turnover. If, on the other hand, AI assistance reduces stress, then workers may be more

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: likely to stay.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: Here, we examine how the deployment of the AI tool impacts worker attrition. For this analysis,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: we compare agents who are never treated with treated agents after treatment. In particular, we drop

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: observations for treated agents prior to treatment because this group experiences no attrition in

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: this period by construction (they must survive to be treated in the future). Our analysis compares

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: the trajectories of agents with the same tenure but diﬀerent access to AI assistance, controlling for

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: location and time ﬁxed eﬀects.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: Column 1 of Table 5 reports the main eﬀect of the AI assistant on attrition. We ﬁnd that,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: on average, the likelihood that a worker leaves in the current month goes down by 8.6 percentage

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: points. Figure 14 considers how these patterns depend on an agent’s tenure or skill at the time the AI

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: system is introduced. We ﬁnd the strongest reductions in attrition among newer agents, those with

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: less than 6 months of experience. The magnitude of this coeﬃcient, around 10 percentage points,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: is large given baseline attrition rates for newer workers of about 25 percent. We caution that this

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: eﬀect may be overstated if access to the AI tool is more likely to be given to agents whom the ﬁrm

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 21 页
sources.quote: deems more likely to stay. Without agent-ﬁxed eﬀects in our speciﬁcation, we cannot account for

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: baseline diﬀerences been treated and untreated agents. In Panel B, we examine attrition by worker

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: skill. Here, we ﬁnd a signiﬁcant decrease in attrition for all skill groups, but no systematic gradient.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote:
4.6.3
Vertical and Horizontal Workﬂow

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: Changes in individual worker-level productivity may have broader implications for organizational

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: workﬂows (Garicano, 2000; Athey et al., 1994; Athey and Stern, 1998). In most ﬁrms, customer

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: support agents are organized both vertically and horizontally. Vertically, front-line agents try to

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: resolve customer problems but can seek the help of supervisors when they are unsure of how to

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: proceed. Customers in our data will sometimes attempt to escalate a conversation by asking to

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: speak to a manager. This type of request generally occurs when the customer feels the current

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: agent is not equipped to address their problem or becomes frustrated. Our data ﬁrm, like most

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: other contact centers, employs designated “escalation agents” to deal with these requests.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: Horizontally, agents often represent speciﬁc departments that handle speciﬁc tasks. For example,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: some may specialize in technical software issues while others specialize in account management

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: issues. A customer with a technical issue requiring that their account be upgraded to a premium

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: product would likely be transferred to a diﬀerent department.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: In Figure 15 and Table 5, we consider the impact of AI model deployment on vertical and

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: horizontal assistance. We do not have a direct measure of whether a call is actually escalated to the

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: manager. Instead, we examine chat-level text data to examine requests for escalations: instances

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: in which a customer requests to speak to a manager or supervisor. In Column 1 of Table 5, we

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: ﬁnd that AI assistance generates an almost 25 percent decline in customer requests to speak to a

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: manager. The accompanying event study is presented in Panel A of Figure 15: we see that declines

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: in requests are persistent and grow over time.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: In contrast, we ﬁnd mixed-to-positive evidence on the impact of access to AI on the number

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: of horizontal transfers to other agents. In Column 2 of Table 5, we see a positively-signed but

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: statistically insigniﬁcant impact on transfers. Panel B of Figure 15 suggests that transfers initially

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: increase but then slowly decline. Upon reviewing the text of these conversations, we see that most

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: transfers appear to redirect customers to a more appropriate department. Many of these transfers

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: occur early in the call, suggesting that transfers reﬂect a matching between a customer’s problem

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: and an agent’s specialty.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: Finally, Appendix Figure A.8 considers how these patterns change by worker skill and tenure.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: Panels A and C focus on requests to speak to a manager. We ﬁnd that these requests are particularly

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 22 页
sources.quote: reduced for agents who were less skilled or less experienced at the time of AI adoption. Panels B

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: and D consider call transfers. Here we ﬁnd mixed results, with positive impacts for some skill and

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: tenure groups and negative impacts for others, but no clear pattern.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote:
5
Conclusion

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: Progress in machine learning opens up a broad set of economic possibilities. Our paper provides

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: the ﬁrst empirical evidence on the eﬀects of a generative AI tool in a real-world workplace. In

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: our setting, we ﬁnd that access to AI-generated recommendations increases worker productivity,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: improves customer sentiment, and is associated with reductions in employee turnover.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: We hypothesize the part of the eﬀect we document is driven by the AI system’s ability to

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: embody the best practices of high-skill workers in our ﬁrm. These practices may have previously

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: been diﬃcult to disseminate because they involve tacit knowledge. Consistent with this, we see that

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: AI assistance leads to substantial improvements in problem resolution and customer satisfaction for

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: newer- and less-skilled workers, but does not help the highest-skilled or most-experienced workers

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: on these measures. Analyzing the text of agent conversations, we ﬁnd suggestive evidence that AI

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: recommendations lead low-skill workers to communicate more like high-skill workers.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: Our ﬁndings, and their limitations, point to a variety of directions for future research.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: As a potential general-purpose technology, generative AI can and will be deployed in a variety of

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: ways, and the eﬀects we ﬁnd may not generalize across all ﬁrms and production processes (Eloundou

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: et al., 2023). For example, our setting has a relatively stable product and set of technical support

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: questions. In areas where the product or environment is changing rapidly, the relative value of AI

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: recommendations—trained on historical data—may be diﬀerent.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: Our results do not capture potential longer-term impacts on skill demand, job design, wages, or

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: customer demand. For example, more eﬀective technical support could accelerate the trend towards

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: contact center agents taking on more complex customer responsibilities, increasing aggregate de-

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: mand even if agents become more productive (Berg et al., 2018; Korinek, 2022). And over the longer

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: term, these tools can uncover patterns and insights that may not be documented in formal channels,

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: changing the way workers are managed or how knowledge is shared within an organization.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: Finally, our ﬁndings raise questions about whether and how workers should be compensated for

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: the data that they provide to AI systems. High-skill workers, in particular, play an important role

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: in model development but see smaller direct beneﬁts in terms of improving their own productivity.

sources.title: generative-ai-work · 第 23 页
sources.quote: Given the early stage of generative AI, these and other questions deserve further scrutiny.
